12	/-! # The Jacobian of a smooth proper curve
13	
14	The Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve over a field, equipped with
15	its structure as an abelian variety.
16	
17	## Status
18	
19	The Jacobian is defined uniformly as the underlying scheme of an Albanese witness
20	(`JacobianWitness`) for the curve `C`; the four protected instances on `Jacobian C` all
21	project from the witness directly.
22	
23	The construction is **uniform in the genus**: the witness is the Picard identity
24	component `Pic⁰_{C/k}` (`picardJacobianWitness`), an abelian variety of dimension
25	`genus C` built by the FGA route (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.*` +
26	`AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.*`). There is **no** genus `= 0` / genus `> 0` split: when
27	`genus C = 0` the tangent space `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is `0`-dimensional, so `Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k`
28	falls out automatically. The former separate `genusZeroWitness` lane (with its
29	`RigidityKbar` / cotangent-vanishing / Frobenius / `ℙ¹`-identification machinery) was a
30	pre-FGA local optimisation and has been removed.
31	
32	`picardJacobianWitness` is wired to the `Pic⁰_{C/k}` development: the witness scheme
33	is `Scheme.Pic0Scheme C`, and its four structural fields are the theorems of
34	`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`. Be precise about what that buys, because
35	"invoked upstream" is not "proved upstream": of those four, `Pic0.grpObj` and
36	`Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible` are proved, while **`Pic0.smooth` and `Pic0.proper`
37	are themselves `sorry`-bodied**. So the witness reaches **five** open obligations,
38	not three: those two upstream, plus the three leaves below, which are the ones new
39	here. Proving only the three would leave `sorryAx` in the witness — verified with
40	`scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`.
41	
42	One of the five is of a different *kind* from the other four, and the difference decides what
43	can be done about it. `Pic0.smooth`, `Pic0.proper` and leaves B and C are *unproved*: each is
44	a true statement awaiting a proof. Leaf A is *false* over a general base field, so
45	`picardJacobianWitness` rests on an inconsistent hypothesis and its consequences are
46	vacuously true — a state no axiom check can distinguish from an honest one. Over an
47	algebraically closed field that leaf is a theorem
48	(`hasRationalPoint_of_curve_of_isAlgClosed`), and `picardJacobianWitnessOfIsAlgClosed`
49	assembles the same witness with it supplied rather than assumed. That is the version of the
50	headline whose open obligations are all of the ordinary kind.
51	
52	What that does *not* do is reduce the count, and the tempting arithmetic here is wrong.
53	`Scheme.Pic0Scheme` carries `[Scheme.HasPicScheme C]`, whose sole producer is the
54	`sorry`-bodied `Scheme.instHasPicScheme`. Over a general field that gate is reached *through*
55	leaf A, so counting it separately looks like double-counting; discharging leaf A makes it
56	*fire* rather than removing it, and it stands free over `k̄`. So the obligations over `k̄`
57	number five as well — `instHasPicScheme`, `Pic0.smooth`, `Pic0.proper`, leaves B and C — with
58	the difference that all five are true. `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean` §0b measures this instead
59	of asserting it.
60	
61	The three leaves are each stated at exactly the strength the assembly consumes:
62	
63	- `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` — the one genuine hypothesis gap: a `k`-rational point on
64	  `C`, which the challenge hypotheses do not give and which is false in general. It is a
65	  gap marker to be *replaced*, not proved (see the leaf's docstring). The former
66	  combined leaf also asserted geometric integrality; that half is now the theorem
67	  `geometricallyIntegral_of_curve`, so the gap is exactly the rational point. Over an
68	  algebraically closed field the gap closes outright:
69	  `hasRationalPoint_of_curve_of_isAlgClosed` is a theorem with clean axioms, so the leaf
70	  is a gap only over a general base field, and `picardJacobianWitnessOfIsAlgClosed`
71	  assembles the witness over `k̄` with it supplied rather than assumed — five obligations
72	  still, but every one of them true.
73	- `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0` — bare smoothness of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` refined to
74	  relative dimension `genus C`. Note this refines `Pic0.smooth`, which is itself
75	  unproved, so the leaf presupposes an obligation rather than resting on one.
76	  `finrank_tangentSpace_pic0_eq_genus` measures what remains: the *dimension count*
77	  `dim T_e Pic⁰_{C/k} = genus C` is landed mathematics and holds here with no transport,
78	  so the leaf owes `Pic0.smooth` plus a translation between two invariants of smoothness
79	  — the tangent-space dimension and the rank of `Ω`, which is what Mathlib's
80	  presentation-based `SmoothOfRelativeDimension` is characterised by — and nothing else.
81	- `isAlbanese_pic0` — the Albanese universal property over an arbitrary base field and
82	  for every marked point, where the landed proof covers the algebraically closed,
83	  positive-genus case. `isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed` measures the distance exactly:
84	  in that case the universal property *is* the landed
85	  `Albanese.Pic0.albanese_universal_property` with no transport, and what the leaf adds
86	  is arbitrary base field, genus `0`, and the basepoint condition `P ≫ ι_P = η`.
87	
88	The file contains:
89	- `IsAlbanese`: the Albanese universal property for a pointed curve.
90	- `IsAlbanese.unique`: uniqueness of the Albanese object up to canonical isomorphism.
91	- `JacobianWitness`: a bundled candidate Albanese object together with the universal
92	  property uniformly over the choice of $k$-rational marked point.
93	- `geometricallyIntegral_of_curve`: the Picard development's `GeometricallyIntegral`
94	  hypothesis, derived from the challenge hypotheses.
95	- `finrank_tangentSpace_pic0_eq_genus` and `isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed`: the parts of
96	  leaves B and C that the landed development already proves, stated at the headline so
97	  that each leaf's remaining distance is compiler-checked rather than described.
98	- `hasRationalPoint_of_curve_of_isAlgClosed` and `picardJacobianWitnessOfIsAlgClosed`:
99	  leaf A discharged over an algebraically closed field, and the witness assembled without
100	  the inconsistent leaf. Unlike the two companions above the first of these is axiom-clean
101	  and is a discharge rather than a record of distance.
102	- `picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint`: the assembly itself, with the rational point
103	  as a hypothesis rather than a source. Both witnesses below are `haveI` specialisations of
104	  it, so neither repeats a field, and it is the compiled form of branch (1) of the open
105	  decision — a headline carrying `C(k) ≠ ∅` needs no new mathematics beyond this. Branch
106	  (2) is not reachable from it; see its docstring.
107	- the three leaves above, and `picardJacobianWitness`, the Albanese witness
108	  `J = Pic⁰_{C/k}` assembled from them with no `sorry` of its own.
109	- `nonempty_jacobianWitness`: existence of an Albanese witness for every curve,
110	  delegating to `picardJacobianWitness`.
111	- `Jacobian` and its four protected instances, each obtained by projection from the
112	  Albanese witness.
113	
114	### Forbidden shortcut (sanity check)
115	
116	Defining `Jacobian C := 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k)))` *unconditionally* (the terminal object,
117	i.e. `Spec k`) compiles and discharges three of the four instances for free, but the
118	fourth instance `SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (𝟙_ _).hom` would force `genus C = 0`,
119	which is mathematically wrong for any curve of genus `≥ 1`. The terminal-object definition
120	is therefore forbidden when `genus C > 0`. The witness-based definition avoids this
121	issue: the witness's `J` is `Pic⁰_{C/k}`, which is `Spec k` exactly when `genus C = 0`
122	and the honest Albanese object otherwise.
123	-/

130	
131	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

133	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))

138	/-- The Albanese universal property for a pointed smooth proper curve `(C, P)`.
139	An object `J` (with abelian-variety structure) is the Albanese of `(C, P)` if it
140	receives a universal pointed morphism `C ⟶ J` sending `P` to the identity. -/
141	def IsAlbanese (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
142	    (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
143	    [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] : Prop :=
144	  ∃ α : C ⟶ J, P ≫ α = η[J] ∧
145	    ∀ {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom]
146	      [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (_ : P ≫ f = η[A]),
147	      ∃! (g : J ⟶ A), f = α ≫ g
148	
149	namespace IsAlbanese
150	
151	noncomputable def ofCurve {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
152	    {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom]
153	    [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] (h : IsAlbanese C P J) : C ⟶ J :=
154	  Classical.choose h
155	
156	lemma comp_ofCurve {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
157	    {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom]
158	    [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] (h : IsAlbanese C P J) :
159	    P ≫ h.ofCurve = η[J] :=
160	  (Classical.choose_spec h).1
161	
162	lemma exists_unique_ofCurve_comp {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
163	    {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom]
164	    [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] (h : IsAlbanese C P J)
165	    {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom]
166	    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (hf : P ≫ f = η[A]) :
167	    ∃! (g : J ⟶ A), f = h.ofCurve ≫ g :=
168	  (Classical.choose_spec h).2 f hf

170	/-- The Albanese object is unique up to a unique isomorphism compatible with the
171	universal morphisms. -/
172	theorem unique {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C}
173	    {J₁ J₂ : Over (Spec (.of k))}
174	    [GrpObj J₁] [IsProper J₁.hom] [Smooth J₁.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J₁.hom]
175	    [GrpObj J₂] [IsProper J₂.hom] [Smooth J₂.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J₂.hom]
176	    (h₁ : IsAlbanese C P J₁) (h₂ : IsAlbanese C P J₂) :

179	  have ⟨h, hh_eq, hh_unique⟩ := h₂.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp h₁.ofCurve h₁.comp_ofCurve

9	/-!
10	# The étale plus construction of the relative Picard functor on affine tests
11	
12	For a curve `C` over `k` and an affine test scheme `Spec A`, the étale-sheafified relative
13	Picard group is computed by a *single* plus construction (the relative Picard presheaf is
14	étale-separated, by descent — proved separately): a class of the plus is represented by a
15	relative Picard class on an étale cover `Spec B → Spec A` equipped with a *descent
16	condition* — equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double cover
17	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B)` — and two representatives are identified when they agree on a common
18	refinement.
19	
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentClasses C E`: the subgroup of `relPic C (Spec B)` of classes
21	  satisfying the descent condition on the cover `E` with carrier `B`.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap C h`: transport of descent classes along a refinement map
23	  `h` of covers.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap_congr` (**the keystone**): a descent class restricts
25	  equally along any two `A`-algebra maps out of the cover carrier — the pair `(j₁, j₂)`
26	  factors through the double cover, where the descent condition kills the difference.
27	  Specialized to refinement maps as `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap_congr`, this is what
28	  makes the colimit below independent of all choices; applied across base rings
29	  (`Picard/PicEtAffMap.lean`), it is also what makes the plus functorial in the test
30	  algebra.
31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff C A`: the one-step plus — descent classes on some cover,
32	  modulo agreement on a common refinement — with its `CommGroup` structure and the
33	  constructor/eliminator API `PicEtAff.mk`, `PicEtAff.ind`, `PicEtAff.mk_eq_mk_iff`,
34	  `PicEtAff.mk_descentMap`.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.unit`: the unit `relPic C (Spec A) →* PicEtAff C A` of the
36	  plus construction — a class pulled back to the trivial cover with its tautological
37	  descent datum.
38	
39	The functoriality of `PicEtAff` in `A` (restriction along test maps, via base change of
40	covers) and the comparison theorems (injectivity of the unit = separatedness; bijectivity
41	under a section = rigidification) are subsequent layers, consuming only this interface.
42	-/

44	set_option autoImplicit false
45	
46	universe u
47	
48	open CategoryTheory
49	
50	open scoped TensorProduct
51	
52	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
53	
54	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
55	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
56	
57	noncomputable section
58	
59	/-! ## Descent classes on an étale cover -/
60	
61	/-- The first coprojection from the carrier of a cover into its self-tensor product over
62	the base — the algebra face of the first projection of the double cover
63	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B) → Spec B` — as a `k`-algebra map. -/
64	def doubleInl (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
65	    E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
66	  Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft
67	
68	/-- The second coprojection into the self-tensor product; see `doubleInl`. -/
69	def doubleInr (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
70	    E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
71	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight).restrictScalars k
72	
73	/-- The subgroup of relative Picard classes on an étale cover of the test algebra
74	satisfying the descent condition: equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double
75	cover. -/
76	def descentClasses (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
77	    Subgroup (relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
78	  MonoidHom.eqLocus
79	    (relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E))
80	    (relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E))
81	
82	lemma mem_descentClasses_iff {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
83	    {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)} :
84	    x ∈ descentClasses C E ↔
85	      relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E) x
86	        = relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E) x :=
87	  Iff.rfl

89	/-! ## Transport along refinement maps -/
90	
91	private lemma doubleInl_comp {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
92	    (doubleInl F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)
93	      = ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E) := by
94	  ext x
95	  simp [doubleInl]
96	
97	private lemma doubleInr_comp {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
98	    (doubleInr F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)
99	      = ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E) := by
100	  ext x
101	  simp [doubleInr]
102	
103	/-- The descent condition is natural in the cover: pullback along a refinement map sends
104	descent classes to descent classes. -/
105	lemma relPicAlgMap_mem_descentClasses {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
106	    (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)}
107	    (hx : x ∈ descentClasses C E) :
108	    relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x ∈ descentClasses C F := by
109	  rw [mem_descentClasses_iff] at hx ⊢
110	  calc relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl F) (relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x)
111	      = relPicAlgMap C ((doubleInl F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)) x :=
112	        (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x).symm
113	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp
114	          (doubleInl E)) x := by rw [doubleInl_comp h]
115	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k)
116	          (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl E) x) := relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x
117	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k)
118	          (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr E) x) := by rw [hx]
119	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp
120	          (doubleInr E)) x := (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x).symm
121	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((doubleInr F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)) x := by
122	        rw [doubleInr_comp h]
123	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr F) (relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x) :=
124	        relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x
125	
126	/-- Transport of descent classes along a refinement map of covers. -/
127	def descentMap {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
128	    descentClasses C E →* descentClasses C F :=
129	  ((relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k)).comp (descentClasses C E).subtype).codRestrict _
130	    fun x => relPicAlgMap_mem_descentClasses C h x.2
131	
132	@[simp]
133	lemma descentMap_coe {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
134	    (x : descentClasses C E) :
135	    (descentMap C h x : relPic C (overSpec k F.Carrier))
136	      = relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
137	  rfl
138	
139	@[simp]
140	lemma descentMap_id {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (x : descentClasses C E) :
141	    descentMap C (AlgHom.id A E.Carrier) x = x := by
142	  ext
143	  rw [descentMap_coe,
144	    show (AlgHom.id A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k = AlgHom.id k E.Carrier from rfl]
145	  exact relPicAlgMap_id C _
146	
147	lemma descentMap_comp {E F G : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
148	    (h' : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier) (x : descentClasses C E) :
149	    descentMap C (h'.comp h) x = descentMap C h' (descentMap C h x) := by
150	  ext
151	  rw [descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe,
152	    show (h'.comp h).restrictScalars k
153	      = (h'.restrictScalars k).comp (h.restrictScalars k) from rfl]
154	  exact relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _
155	
156	/-- **Generalized refinement-map independence**, the keystone of the plus construction:
157	a class satisfying the descent condition restricts equally along any two `A`-algebra maps
158	out of the cover carrier — into an arbitrary test algebra, not merely another cover.  The
159	pair `(j₁, j₂)` factors jointly through the double cover of the source, where the descent
160	condition identifies the two pullbacks. -/
161	theorem relPicAlgMap_congr {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A} {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
162	    [Algebra k R] [Algebra A R] [IsScalarTower k A R] (j₁ j₂ : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] R)
163	    {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)} (hx : x ∈ descentClasses C E) :
164	    relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x = relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x := by
165	  set H : E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier →ₐ[A] R :=
166	    Algebra.TensorProduct.lift j₁ j₂ fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _ with hH
167	  have key₁ : (H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E) = j₁.restrictScalars k := by
168	    ext y
169	    simp [hH, doubleInl]
170	  have key₂ : (H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E) = j₂.restrictScalars k := by
171	    ext y
172	    simp [hH, doubleInr]
173	  calc relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x
174	      = relPicAlgMap C ((H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E)) x := by rw [key₁]
175	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (H.restrictScalars k) (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl E) x) :=
176	        relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _
177	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (H.restrictScalars k) (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr E) x) := by
178	        have hx' : relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E) x
179	            = relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E) x := hx
180	        rw [hx']
181	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E)) x :=
182	        (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _).symm
183	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x := by rw [key₂]
184	
185	/-- **Refinement-map independence**: any two refinement maps between the same covers
186	transport descent classes identically — what makes the plus construction independent of
187	all choices. -/
188	theorem descentMap_congr {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
189	    (h₁ h₂ : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) (x : descentClasses C E) :
190	    descentMap C h₁ x = descentMap C h₂ x :=
191	  Subtype.ext (relPicAlgMap_congr C h₁ h₂ x.2)
192	
193	/-! ## The plus construction -/
194	
195	/-- Two descent-class representatives are identified when they agree after transport to a
196	common refinement.  By `descentMap_congr` the choice of transport maps is immaterial, so
197	the relation is an equivalence (directedness of covers gives transitivity). -/
198	instance picEtAffSetoid : Setoid (Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E) where
199	  r p q := ∃ (F : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (f : p.1.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
200	    (g : q.1.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier), descentMap C f p.2 = descentMap C g q.2
201	  iseqv := by
202	    constructor
203	    · exact fun p => ⟨p.1, AlgHom.id A _, AlgHom.id A _, rfl⟩
204	    · rintro p q ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩
205	      exact ⟨F, g, f, hfg.symm⟩
206	    · rintro p q r ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩ ⟨G, f', g', hfg'⟩
207	      refine ⟨F.prod G, (F.prodInl G).comp f, (F.prodInr G).comp g', ?_⟩
208	      rw [descentMap_comp, descentMap_comp, hfg, ← descentMap_comp, ← descentMap_comp,
209	        descentMap_congr C ((F.prodInl G).comp g) ((F.prodInr G).comp f') q.2,
210	        descentMap_comp, hfg', ← descentMap_comp]
211	
212	variable (A) in
213	/-- The one-step étale plus of the relative Picard functor at the affine test `Spec A`:
214	relative Picard classes on some presented étale cover satisfying the descent condition,
215	modulo agreement on a common refinement.  On affine tests this *is* the étale
216	sheafification of the relative Picard presheaf (one plus suffices because the presheaf is
217	étale-separated — proved separately). -/
218	def PicEtAff : Type u :=
219	  Quotient (picEtAffSetoid C (A := A))
220	
221	namespace PicEtAff
222	
223	/-- The plus class of a relative Picard class with a descent condition on a cover. -/
224	def mk (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E) : PicEtAff C A :=
225	  Quotient.mk _ ⟨E, x⟩
226	
227	@[elab_as_elim]
228	theorem ind {motive : PicEtAff C A → Prop}
229	    (mk : ∀ (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E), motive (mk C E x)) :
230	    ∀ q, motive q := by
231	  intro q
232	  induction q using Quotient.ind with
233	  | _ p => exact mk p.1 p.2

235	theorem mk_eq_mk_iff {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} {x : descentClasses C E}
236	    {y : descentClasses C F} :
237	    mk C E x = mk C F y ↔
238	      ∃ (G : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier)
239	        (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier), descentMap C f x = descentMap C g y :=
240	  Quotient.eq

242	/-- Transporting the representative to a finer cover does not change the plus class. -/
243	@[simp]
244	theorem mk_descentMap {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
245	    (x : descentClasses C E) : mk C F (descentMap C h x) = mk C E x :=
246	  Quotient.sound ⟨F, AlgHom.id A F.Carrier, h, by rw [descentMap_id]⟩
247	
248	/-! ### The group structure -/
249	
250	/-- Transport through a `prodLift` collapses on the left factor. -/
251	lemma descentMap_prodLift_inl {E F H : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
252	    (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier) (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier)
253	    (x : descentClasses C E) :
254	    descentMap C (Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift f g) (descentMap C (E.prodInl F) x)
255	      = descentMap C f x := by
256	  rw [← descentMap_comp, Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift_comp_prodInl]
257	
258	/-- Transport through a `prodLift` collapses on the right factor. -/
259	lemma descentMap_prodLift_inr {E F H : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
260	    (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier) (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier)
261	    (y : descentClasses C F) :
262	    descentMap C (Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift f g) (descentMap C (E.prodInr F) y)
263	      = descentMap C g y := by
264	  rw [← descentMap_comp, Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift_comp_prodInr]

266	set_option maxHeartbeats 4000000 in
267	-- The `rw` chain unifies `descentMap` nests whose `AlgHom` instance arguments run through

269	private lemma mulLift_compat (p q p' q' : Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E)

271	    mk C (p.1.prod q.1)

275	          * descentMap C (p'.1.prodInr q'.1) q'.2) := by

277	  obtain ⟨G, g, g', hg⟩ := hq

279	    Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift ((F.prodInl G).comp f) ((F.prodInr G).comp g),
280	    Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift ((F.prodInl G).comp f') ((F.prodInr G).comp g'), ?_⟩

282	    descentMap_prodLift_inl, descentMap_prodLift_inr, descentMap_comp, descentMap_comp,

9	/-!
10	# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)
11	
12	For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
13	arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
14	of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
15	comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
16	`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
19	  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
21	  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
22	  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
23	  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
25	  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
27	  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
28	  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
29	  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
30	  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
31	  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
32	  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
33	-/
34	
35	set_option autoImplicit false
36	
37	universe u
38	
39	open CategoryTheory
40	
41	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
42	
43	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
44	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
45	
46	noncomputable section
47	
48	/-! ## The degree at a field point -/
49	
50	/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
51	`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
52	algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
53	restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
54	def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
55	    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
56	  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
57	
58	section DegAt
59	
60	variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
61	
62	/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
63	@[simp]
64	theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
65	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
66	  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
67	
68	/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
69	theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
70	    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
71	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
72	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
73	        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
74	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]
75	
76	/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
77	theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
78	    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
79	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
80	  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
81	  rfl
82	
83	/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
84	restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
85	field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
86	degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
87	theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
88	    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
89	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
90	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
91	  rw [← picEtMap_comp]
92	
93	/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
94	theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
95	    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
96	    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
97	  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'
98	
99	end DegAt
100	
101	/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/
102	
103	variable (C) in
104	/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
105	classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
106	degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
107	def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
108	  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
109	    degAt lam t = 0}
110	  one_mem' := by
111	    intro K _ _ t
112	    exact degAt_one t
113	  mul_mem' := by
114	    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
115	    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
116	  inv_mem' := by
117	    intro a ha K _ _ t
118	    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]
119	
120	/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
121	theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
122	    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
123	      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
124	          degAt lam t = 0 :=
125	  Iff.rfl
126	
127	variable (C) in
128	/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
129	of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
130	definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
131	points. -/
132	def pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
133	    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=
134	  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')
135	    fun lam K _ _ t' => (degAt_picEtMap f (lam : picEt C T) t').trans (lam.2 K (t' ≫ f))
136	
137	/-- The underlying étale Picard class of a restricted degree-zero class — the
138	naturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/
139	@[simp]
140	theorem pic0Map_coe {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
141	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :
142	    (pic0Map C f lam : picEt C T') = picEtMap C f (lam : picEt C T) :=
143	  rfl
144	
145	variable (C) in
146	/-- **The degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
147	subfunctor of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor `picEtFunctor C` of classes
148	of degree zero at every field point of the test object.  This is the binding carrier of
149	the Wave-4 representability statement (design §2.7): the Jacobian represents *this*
150	functor. -/
151	def pic0Functor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
152	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop)
153	  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Map C g.unop)
154	  map_id T := by
155	    ext lam U
156	    exact congrArg (fun z : picEt C T.unop => z.1 U) (picEtMap_id C (lam : picEt C T.unop))
157	  map_comp g h := by
158	    ext lam U
159	    exact congrArg (fun z => z.1 U) (picEtMap_comp C g.unop h.unop (lam : picEt C _))
160	
161	@[simp]
162	theorem pic0Functor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
163	    (pic0Functor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :=
164	  rfl
165	
166	@[simp]
167	theorem pic0Functor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
168	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
169	    (pic0Functor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
170	  rfl
171	
172	variable (C) in
173	/-- The inclusion of the degree-zero subfunctor into the étale-sheafified relative
174	Picard functor, as a natural transformation — the naturality square consumers cite
175	(bundled form of `pic0Map_coe`). -/
176	def pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C where
177	  app T := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Subgroup C T.unop).subtype
178	  naturality _ _ _ := rfl
179	
180	end

10	
11	The usable form of the (C1) étale-separatedness theorem
12	(`AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.unit_injective`, `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.CechKernelLemma`)
13	for the Layer-2 gluing arguments: for a curve `C` (proper, geometrically irreducible and
14	geometrically reduced over `k`), a `k`-algebra `R` and a presented étale cover `E` of
15	`Spec R`, two relative Picard classes over `R` with equal restrictions to the cover
16	carrier are equal (`AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap_injective_of_etaleCover`).
17	
18	Indeed, the unit of the plus construction sends a class `z` to its tautological descent
19	class represented on *any* cover (`PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk`), so equal restrictions give
20	equal units, and the unit is injective by (C1).
21	-/

27	open CategoryTheory
28	
29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
30	
31	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))

34	/-- The composite `R → Γ(self cover) → Γ(E)` of the tautological identifications is the
35	structure map of the carrier of `E`. -/
36	private lemma fromSelf_comp_ofId (E : Algebra.EtaleCover R) :
37	    (E.fromSelf.restrictScalars k).comp
38	        ((Algebra.ofId R (Algebra.EtaleCover.self R).Carrier).restrictScalars k)
39	      = (Algebra.ofId R E.Carrier).restrictScalars k := by
40	  ext r
41	  simp only [AlgHom.coe_comp, AlgHom.coe_restrictScalars', Function.comp_apply,
42	    Algebra.ofId_apply, Algebra.EtaleCover.fromSelf, AlgHom.coe_comp]
43	  exact congrArg (algebraMap R E.Carrier)
44	    (((Algebra.EtaleCover.selfEquiv R).commutes r).trans rfl)
45	
46	/-- The unit of the plus construction, represented on an arbitrary cover: `unit z` is the
47	class of the tautological descent datum of `z` on any presented étale cover `E`. -/
48	theorem PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk (E : Algebra.EtaleCover R) (z : relPic C (overSpec k R)) :
49	    PicEtAff.unit C R z
50	      = PicEtAff.mk C E
51	          ⟨relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.ofId R E.Carrier).restrictScalars k) z,
52	            tautological_mem_descentClasses C E z⟩ := by
53	  have hval : descentMap C E.fromSelf
54	        ⟨relPicAlgMap C
55	            ((Algebra.ofId R (Algebra.EtaleCover.self R).Carrier).restrictScalars k) z,
56	          tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self R) z⟩
57	      = ⟨relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.ofId R E.Carrier).restrictScalars k) z,
58	          tautological_mem_descentClasses C E z⟩ := by
59	    refine Subtype.ext ?_
60	    rw [descentMap_coe, ← relPicAlgMap_comp, fromSelf_comp_ofId]
61	  calc PicEtAff.unit C R z
62	      = PicEtAff.mk C (.self R)
63	          ⟨relPicAlgMap C
64	              ((Algebra.ofId R (Algebra.EtaleCover.self R).Carrier).restrictScalars k) z,
65	            tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self R) z⟩ := rfl
66	    _ = PicEtAff.mk C E (descentMap C E.fromSelf
67	          ⟨relPicAlgMap C
68	              ((Algebra.ofId R (Algebra.EtaleCover.self R).Carrier).restrictScalars k) z,
69	            tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self R) z⟩) :=
70	        (PicEtAff.mk_descentMap C E.fromSelf _).symm
71	    _ = PicEtAff.mk C E
72	          ⟨relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.ofId R E.Carrier).restrictScalars k) z,
73	            tautological_mem_descentClasses C E z⟩ := by rw [hval]
74

80	licenses every gluing step of the Layer-2 functor. -/

86	  rw [PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk C E x, PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk C E y]
87	  exact congrArg (PicEtAff.mk C E) (Subtype.ext h)

/-!

# The étale site

In this file we define the big étale site, i.e. the étale topology as a Grothendieck topology
on the category of schemes.

-/

@[expose] public section

universe v u

open CategoryTheory MorphismProperty Limits

namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

/-- Big étale site: the étale precoverage on the category of schemes. -/
def etalePrecoverage : Precoverage Scheme.{u} :=
  precoverage @Etale

/-- Big étale site: the étale pretopology on the category of schemes. -/
def etalePretopology : Pretopology Scheme.{u} :=
  pretopology @Etale

/-- Big étale site: the étale topology on the category of schemes. -/
abbrev etaleTopology : GrothendieckTopology Scheme.{u} :=
  grothendieckTopology @Etale

lemma zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology : zariskiTopology ≤ etaleTopology := by
  apply grothendieckTopology_monotone
  intro X Y f hf
  infer_instance

/-- The small étale site of a scheme is the Grothendieck topology on the
category of schemes étale over `X` induced from the étale topology on `Scheme.{u}`. -/
def smallEtaleTopology (X : Scheme.{u}) : GrothendieckTopology X.Etale :=
  X.smallGrothendieckTopology (P := @Etale)

/-- The pretopology generating the small étale site. -/
def smallEtalePretopology (X : Scheme.{u}) : Pretopology X.Etale :=
  X.smallPretopology (Q := @Etale) (P := @Etale)

instance {S : Scheme.{u}} (𝒰 : S.Cover (precoverage @Etale)) (i : 𝒰.I₀) : Etale (𝒰.f i) :=
  𝒰.map_prop i

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- A separably closed field `Ω` defines a point on the étale topology by the fiber
functor `X ↦ Hom(Spec Ω, X)`. -/
noncomputable
def geometricFiber (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsSepClosed Ω] : etaleTopology.Point where
  fiber := coyoneda.obj ⟨Spec (.of Ω)⟩
  jointly_surjective {S} R hR (f : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) := by
    obtain ⟨⟨x, a⟩, rfl⟩ := (Scheme.SpecToEquivOfField Ω S).symm.surjective f
    rw [mem_grothendieckTopology_iff] at hR
    obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := hR
    obtain ⟨i, y, rfl⟩ := 𝒰.exists_eq x
    refine ⟨𝒰.X i, 𝒰.f i, hle _ _ ⟨i⟩, ?_⟩
    let k := (𝒰.X i).residueField y
    let m : S.residueField (𝒰.f i y) ⟶ (𝒰.X i).residueField y :=
      (𝒰.f i).residueFieldMap y
    algebraize [((𝒰.f i).residueFieldMap y).hom, a.hom]
    let b : (𝒰.X i).residueField y →ₐ[S.residueField (𝒰.f i y)] Ω :=
      IsSepClosed.lift
    have hfac : (𝒰.f i).residueFieldMap y ≫ CommRingCat.ofHom b.toRingHom = a := by
      ext1; exact b.comp_algebraMap
    use Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom b.toRingHom) ≫ (𝒰.X i).fromSpecResidueField y

277	/-! ### The Abel map
278	
279	The class `HasAbelMap` carries the map itself (a data field `abel`), so that
280	`abelMap` has the defining property `abelMap_app_mk` below; the instance
281	supplies the explicit natural transformation `abelMapWitness C`.
282	
283	Construction of `abelMapWitness C : Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)]`:
284	a relative effective divisor family `⟨F, q⟩` on `C ×_k T` has invertible ideal
285	`I_D = ker q`; the Abel map sends its class to
286	`[O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[I_D]`, the additive inverse (in the group-valued target
287	`Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`) of the class of the ideal sheaf.  It is assembled as the
288	composite `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`, where `abelKernelNatTrans` is the
289	substantive `[D] ↦ [I_D]` transformation and `picNeg` is the (natural)
290	negation on the group-valued functor.
291	
292	Naturality of `abelKernelNatTrans` is the mathematical heart: for a test map
293	`g : T' ⟶ T` the base-change square is cartesian (`quotBaseSquare`), and the
294	**kernel–pullback comparison** `g_C^*(ker q) ⟶ ker(g_C^* q)` is an isomorphism
295	under the divisor conditions (`Modules.isIso_pullbackKernelComparison`, whose
296	side hypotheses — epi `q`, quasi-coherent source, finitely-presented `F`,
297	`T`-flat `F`, invertible kernel — are exactly the fields of `DivFamily`), so
298	`ker` commutes with base change and the class `[ker q]` is natural.  Negation
299	is natural because `Pic^♯`'s pullback maps are group homomorphisms.
300	
301	The `dual` route (`Modules.dual (ker q)` as an explicit inverse) is available
302	for the *object-level* invertibility (`dual_isLocallyTrivial`) but is not used
303	here: the group-inverse `-[ker q]` is the canonical `[I_D⁻¹]` and makes
304	naturality rest only on the kernel–pullback comparison, avoiding the
305	not-yet-formalised sheaf-level dual-pullback commutation.
306	
307	Blueprint reference: `lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence` (Kleiman §3
308	Def. `dfn:Abel`); this instance is the **natural-transformation half** — `Div`
309	representability (Kleiman §3 Thm. `th:repDiv`) is NOT claimed here. -/

320	        (⟨kernel y.q, y.kerLocallyTrivial⟩ : LineBundle.OnProduct C.hom T.unop.hom) := by

we first construct a bijection `Sieve.overEquiv Y : Sieve Y ≃ Sieve Y.left`

is covering for `J`. As a result, the forgetful functor

Concretely, `IdentityComponent G` is built from `identityComponentCarrier G`:
the open subscheme of `G` whose underlying topological space is the connected
component of `|G|` through the image of the identity section, with the
inherited structure morphism `(identityComponentCarrier G).ι ≫ G.hom`. The
carrier is `connectedComponent (identitySectionPoint G)`, open by
`isOpen_connectedComponent` under the
`identityComponent_locallyConnectedSpace` instance (EGA I 6.1.9: locally
Noetherian spaces have open connected components). -/
noncomputable def IdentityComponent {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (G : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [GrpObj G] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] :
    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
  Over.mk ((identityComponentCarrier G).ι ≫ G.hom)

/-- **The identity component is an open and closed subgroup scheme.**

The bundled statement of Kleiman §5 Lem.~`lem:agps`~(3): the identity
component `G^0 = IdentityComponent G` of a `k`-group scheme `G` locally of
finite type comes with a morphism `IdentityComponent G ⟶ G` (in
`Over (Spec (.of k))`) whose underlying scheme morphism is both an open
immersion and a closed immersion (i.e. the inclusion of a clopen
subscheme).

The remaining parts of Kleiman's conclusion — the group-subscheme property
(the inclusion is a homomorphism of `k`-group schemes), finite-type-ness over
`k` (`LocallyOfFiniteType` + quasi-compactness), geometric irreducibility and
base-change-commutation — are stated separately as
`IdentityComponent.isSubgroupHomomorphism`,
`IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible` and
`IdentityComponent.baseChangeIso`.

The inclusion morphism is `Over.homMk (identityComponentCarrier G).ι`, with
the over-category compatibility holding by definition of
`IdentityComponent G`. The `.left` of this morphism is
`(identityComponentCarrier G).ι`, an open immersion by the global
`Scheme.Opens.instIsOpenImmersionι` instance. For the closed-immersion
half we apply `IsClosedImmersion.of_isPreimmersion` to the open immersion
and reduce to `IsClosed (↑(identityComponentCarrier G) : Set _)`, which holds
because the carrier is a connected component and connected components are
closed. -/
theorem IdentityComponent.isOpenSubgroupScheme {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (G : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [GrpObj G] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] :
    Nonempty {f : IdentityComponent G ⟶ G //
        IsOpenImmersion f.left ∧ IsClosedImmersion f.left} := by
  -- Over-category compatibility for the underlying open immersion.
  have hcomp : (identityComponentCarrier G).ι ≫ G.hom = (IdentityComponent G).hom := by
    simp [IdentityComponent]
  -- The over-morphism witness.
  let f : IdentityComponent G ⟶ G :=
    Over.homMk (U := IdentityComponent G) (V := G) (identityComponentCarrier G).ι hcomp
  refine ⟨⟨f, ?_, ?_⟩⟩
  · -- `f.left = (identityComponentCarrier G).ι` (definitionally; `Over.homMk_left` simp).
    -- An open immersion by `Scheme.Opens.instIsOpenImmersionι`.
    change IsOpenImmersion (identityComponentCarrier G).ι
theorem IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible
    {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (G : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [GrpObj G] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] :
    LocallyOfFiniteType (IdentityComponent G).hom ∧
      QuasiCompact (IdentityComponent G).hom ∧
      GeometricallyIrreducible (IdentityComponent G).hom := by
  refine ⟨identityComponent_locallyOfFiniteType G, ?_,
    identityComponent_geometricallyIrreducible G⟩
  haveI h : CompactSpace (IdentityComponent G).left := identityComponent_compactSpace G
  exact HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr h

import Mathlib
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RelPicFunctor

/-!
# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor

This file constructs the **étale-sheafified relative Picard functor**
`Pic_{(C/k)ét}` of a smooth proper curve `C/k` and proves that it *is* a sheaf
for the étale topology — the object whose representability is the project's
central open obligation (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).

## Why the sheafification is the right object

The relative Picard presheaf `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`
(`Scheme.PicSharp.relPresheaf`, Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`) is in general **not
a sheaf**, not even for the Zariski topology (Kleiman §2, L1292–L1302): a line
bundle on `C ×_k T` can be trivial on each member of a cover of `T` without
being trivial modulo `π_T^* Pic(T)`, because the gluing data is a `Pic`-class
of the overlaps. Kleiman's representability theorem (§4 Thm. `th:main`) is
therefore a statement about the associated **étale** sheaf, and it is that
statement which is true over an arbitrary base field with no rational-point
hypothesis.

There are two ways to reach a sheaf, and they differ in what has to be
supplied:

1. assume `C` has a `k`-rational point. Then Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 says the
   comparison `Pic_{C/k} → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is already bijective, so the plain
   presheaf is the sheaf. This is *strictly weaker* than the challenge, whose
   curve need not have a rational point, and it is the route the conditional
   `Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` records;
2. sheafify. Nothing is assumed about `C(k)`, and the sheaf axiom holds by
   construction. This is the route realised here and the one the project
   claims (owner decision of 2026-07-28).

## The site

Mathlib `v4.31` carries the big étale site on schemes,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleTopology = grothendieckTopology @Etale`
(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`). The relative Picard presheaf
lives on the slice `Over (Spec k)` rather than on `Scheme`, so the topology is
transported along the localisation of SGA 4 III 5.2.1, available in Mathlib as
`GrothendieckTopology.over`: a sieve of `T : Over (Spec k)` covers iff the
corresponding sieve of `T.left` covers étale-locally. That transport is where
"the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`" becomes a definition rather than a parameter,
and it is what lets the sheaf property below be a *theorem* rather than a
hypothesis.

## Main definitions

* `Scheme.etaleTopologyOver k` — the étale topology on `(Sch/k) = Over (Spec k)`.
* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` — `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, a bundled
  `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`, obtained by sheafifying the
  relative Picard presheaf.
* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf_isSheaf` — the sheaf property, extracted as a
  standalone statement about the underlying presheaf.
* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt C` — the set-valued functor
  `T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)` that the representability obligation is stated
  against, together with `picEtComparison C`, the canonical comparison
  `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` from the unsheafified functor.
* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` — the sheaf property of `picEt`
  itself (the group structure forgotten), which is what a representing scheme
  must match.

## References

Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020), §2 Def. `df:Pfs` (the
étale-sheaf clause) and Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`), §4 Thm. `th:main`.
Blueprint: `def:rel_pic_etale_sheafification`,
`thm:rel_pic_etale_sheaf_group_structure`, `sec:fga_pic_setup`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Scheme

/-! ## §1. The étale site of `(Sch/k)` -/

/-- **The étale topology on `(Sch/k)`.**

The big étale topology on schemes (`Scheme.etaleTopology`, Mathlib
`AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`) localised at `Spec k` along SGA 4
III 5.2.1 (`GrothendieckTopology.over`): a sieve of a `k`-scheme `T` is
covering exactly when the sieve it generates on the underlying scheme
`T.left` is covering for the étale topology
(`GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff`).

This is the site on which the relative Picard presheaf of
`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` lives, so it is the site whose sheafification
produces Kleiman's `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`. Note that the earlier
`PicSharp.etSheaf` of that file takes the topology as a *parameter*, for
want of a canonical choice; this definition supplies the canonical one, and
`PicSharp.etaleSheaf` below is the instantiation. -/
abbrev etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    GrothendieckTopology (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :=
  Scheme.etaleTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))

/-- The étale topology on `(Sch/k)` refines the Zariski one: a Zariski cover
of a `k`-scheme is an étale cover. Transported from
`zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology` through the localisation, which is
monotone because `mem_over_iff` characterises membership by the pushed-forward
sieve on the underlying scheme.

Recorded because it is the precise sense in which sheafifying étale-locally is
*stronger* than sheafifying Zariski-locally: a Zariski sheaf need not be an
étale sheaf, and the relative Picard presheaf is not even the former. -/
theorem zariskiTopologyOver_le_etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) ≤ etaleTopologyOver k := by
  intro T S hS
  rw [GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff] at hS ⊢
  exact Scheme.zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology _ hS

namespace PicSharp

/-! ## §2. The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor -/

/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor** `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`
(Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`, étale-sheaf clause).

The associated étale sheaf of the relative Picard presheaf
`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` (`PicSharp.relPresheaf`), as a bundled object
of `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`. Its sheaf property is not an
assumption but part of the datum — `Sheaf.cond`, extracted as
`etaleSheaf_isSheaf` below — which is the whole point of passing to it: the
unsheafified `relPresheaf` is not a sheaf even Zariski-locally.

This is a genuine instantiation of the parametric `PicSharp.etSheaf` of
`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` at the canonical étale topology, with one
correction: `etSheaf` sheafifies the *absolute* functor `PicSharp.presheaf`
(`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)`), whereas Kleiman's `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` and the
representability theorem are about the *relative* one, `relPresheaf`. It is
the relative functor that is sheafified here.

The abelian-group structure survives sheafification because the target
`AddCommGrpCat` has the sheafification adjunction
(`HasWeakSheafify` for a concrete, filtered-colimit-preserving forgetful
functor); `toEtaleSheaf` below is the unit. -/
noncomputable def etaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
  (CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}).obj
    (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)

/-- **The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, as a standalone statement.**

The underlying presheaf of `PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` satisfies the sheaf axiom
for the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`. This is `Sheaf.cond` of the bundled
object, stated separately because it is the property consumers cite: a
representing scheme for `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` exists only because the functor being
represented is an étale sheaf (a representable functor is a sheaf for any
subcanonical topology, so a non-sheaf can never be representable — which is
exactly why the unsheafified `relPresheaf` needs a rational point).

Proved, not assumed: sheafification produces a sheaf. -/
theorem etaleSheaf_isSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (etaleSheaf C).val :=
  (etaleSheaf C).cond

/-- **The comparison map** `Pic_{C/k} ⟶ Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, i.e. the unit of the
sheafification adjunction at the relative Picard presheaf.

Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`) says this map is an isomorphism when `C` has a
`k`-rational point (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic here). Over an
arbitrary base field it is only a comparison: the honest object is the target,
which is why the representability obligation is stated there. -/
noncomputable def toEtaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ (etaleSheaf C).val :=
  CategoryTheory.toSheafify (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)

/-- The universal property of the sheafification, in the form consumers use:
every morphism from the relative Picard presheaf to (the underlying presheaf
of) an étale sheaf factors uniquely through `toEtaleSheaf`.

This is what makes `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` the *canonical* choice rather than one
sheaf among many, and it is the step that turns a representing scheme for the
sheaf into a universal receiver of relative Picard classes. -/
noncomputable def etaleSheafHomEquiv {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    (G : Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}) :
    (etaleSheaf C ⟶ G) ≃ (PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ G.val) :=
  ((CategoryTheory.sheafificationAdjunction (etaleTopologyOver k)
    AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}).homEquiv (PicSharp.relPresheaf C) G)

end PicSharp

namespace PicScheme

/-! ## §3. The set-valued functor that gets represented -/

/-- **The functor whose representability is the project's central obligation**:
the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor with its group structure
forgotten,

```
picEt C : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1),   T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T).
```

Representability is a statement about the underlying set-valued functor; the
group structure is transported back onto the representing scheme by Yoneda
(`PicScheme.groupSchemeStructure`), exactly as for the unsheafified
`picSharp`.

Contrast with `picSharp C = relPresheaf C ⋙ forget`: that functor is
representable only under a rational-point hypothesis (it is not even a
Zariski sheaf otherwise), whereas *this* one is the object of Kleiman §4
Thm. `th:main` and its representability needs no hypothesis on `C(k)`. -/
noncomputable def picEt {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1) :=
  (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).val ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}

/-- The comparison `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` of set-valued functors, the
set-level shadow of `PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf`. An isomorphism under a
`k`-rational point (Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5), a comparison in general. -/
noncomputable def picEtComparison {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    picSharp C ⟶ picEt C :=
  CategoryTheory.whiskerRight (PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf C)
    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})

/-- **`picEt` is an étale sheaf of sets.**

The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` survives forgetting the group structure,
because the forgetful functor `AddCommGrpCat ⥤ Type` preserves the limits the
sheaf condition is stated by. Together with the fact that a representable
functor is a sheaf for a subcanonical topology, this is the structural reason
the representability obligation is *consistent* as stated — which the
unsheafified `picSharp` version was not, absent a rational point. -/
theorem picEt_isSheaf_forget {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    Presieve.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (picEt C) :=
  (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).cond

end PicScheme

end Scheme

end AlgebraicGeometry
